cards.explanation: The answer is False. Job did go quiet earlier (Job 40:4, 5), but his silence doesn't end anything. The LORD says, “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.” (Job 40:7) So Job isn't off the hook yet, friends. He's being asked to answer.

The word is justify. The LORD asks, “Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?” (Job 40:8) That's the whole question, friends. Would Job put God in the wrong just to come out looking right? It's a big question, so read it slowly.

The answer is to look on him and bring him low. The LORD says, “Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.” (Job 40:12) Earlier He says to “look on every proud man and bring him low.” (Job 40:11) It's a huge job, friends, and I'd be hiding behind my apron.

The answer is that Job's own right hand can save him. The LORD says, “Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.” (Job 40:14) Notice the "then." It comes after the LORD's whole list of challenges: an arm like God's, a voice that thunders, humbling the proud and trampling the wicked. (Job 40:9 to 13) The confession is only on the table if Job could pull all of that off.
The word is grass. The LORD says, “He feeds on grass like an ox.” (Job 40:15) His bones are tubes of bronze, and he's out there grazing. That's one calm creature, friends.
The answer is his Maker. The LORD says of Behemoth, “only his Maker can draw the sword against him.” (Job 40:19) Nobody else is on that list, friends. Not one name.

The answer is False. The text says, “The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.” (Job 40:20) The beasts play nearby, which is the opposite of running and hiding. The second half of that statement is where it goes wrong.

The answer is True. “Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.” (Job 40:23) Raging water doesn't rattle him. The Jordan surges all the way up to his mouth, and he stays secure. Friends, I'd be doing laps on my gold base.

The answer is whether anyone can capture him. The LORD asks, “Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?” (Job 40:24) The question is about catching him, friends. And the question answers itself.

The answer is whether Job could tame and control him. Hooks, cords, leashes, even making him a slave for life. (Job 41:1-5) Every question is about whether Job could bring Leviathan under his control. Question after question, same direction, friends.

The word is battle. The LORD says, “If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!” (Job 41:8) One try is all it takes, friends. Nobody signs up for a second round. That's a lesson you only need once.

The question is, who is able to stand against Me. The LORD says, “No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?” (Job 41:10) He goes from the creature straight to Himself. If no one is fierce enough to rouse Leviathan, who could stand against the One who says, “Everything under heaven is Mine.”? (Job 41:11)

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.” (Job 41:11) God owes nobody, friends, because everything under heaven is already His. The question answers itself.

The answer is that they're so tight no air can pass between them. The LORD says, “One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.” (Job 41:16) That's armor with no gaps, friends, and no gaps means nothing slips through. The next verse says, “They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.” (Job 41:17) Tight and sealed together is the picture.

The answer is True. “Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!” (Job 41:19) And “Smoke billows from his nostrils…” (Job 41:20) Verse 21 adds, “…flames pour from his mouth.” (Job 41:21) Fire out the mouth and smoke out the nose, friends.

The answer is False, and the statement falls apart at the arrow. “No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.” (Job 41:28) The sword, the spear, the dart and the arrow have no effect on him. (Job 41:26) So the arrow does nothing to him either, friends.

The answer is that nothing on earth is his equal. The LORD says, “Nothing on earth is his equal…” (Job 41:33) He says it plainly, friends. Leviathan is one of a kind, and nothing on earth matches him. That's how the LORD sums him up.

The word is proud. The LORD says, “He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.” (Job 41:34) Remember the LORD told Job to look on every proud man. (Job 40:12) Here is a creature who already looks down on them all, friends. Leviathan looks down on the very ones the LORD told Job to humble.

The answer is that God can do all things. Job says, “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.” (Job 42:2) After all those questions, friends, that's where he begins. Nobody can block God's plans.

The answer is True. Job says, “Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.” (Job 42:3) He's quoting the LORD's earlier question first, friends. Then he owns up to it himself.

The answer is that before he'd heard of God but now he's seen Him. Job says, “My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.” (Job 42:5) Before, he had heard of God. Now he says he has seen Him. Friends, it's like the difference between reading a recipe and smelling the cookies in the oven.

The word is repents. Job says, “Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.” (Job 42:6) It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's a heavy moment. Just before it, he says he has seen God. (Job 42:5)
